title: The one you laugh at may be better than you.
subtitle: Mockery, digs, and names people hate
then: Abu Jabirah said this was revealed about Banu Salamah. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, many of them had two or three nicknames. {trap}He would call a man by one and be told, he hates that name.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links mockery to the hadith: arrogance is rejecting truth and {trap}belittling people.{/trap}
now: The nickname from school that still sticks at family weddings. The office group that has a running joke about one colleague's accent. The meme you share about someone's weight. {idea}The person in the joke may be closer to Allah than everyone laughing.{/idea}
old: It is just banter, they know I do not mean it.
new: If they dislike the name or the joke, it is not banter, and they may be better than me.
try: Stop using one nickname today that someone has ever winced at. Call them by their real name.

title: Suspicion, spying, backbiting: three steps down one road.
subtitle: How a bad guess becomes a feast on someone's honor
then: The Prophet ﷺ was asked what backbiting is. {trap}Mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes,{/trap} he said, and if it is untrue it is slander. Umar said never think ill of a believer's word while you can find a good excuse for it. The verse ends with hope: {reward}Allah accepts repentance and is Merciful.{/reward}
now: Your colleague leaves early three days in a row. You guess why, check their social media, then mention it over lunch. {trap}Each step felt small.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to stop at the first one: a kinder guess.{/idea}
old: I am not lying, I am just saying what I noticed.
new: Saying true things someone would hate to hear behind their back is still eating at their honor.
try: The next time you start to speak about someone absent, ask: would I say this with them here? If not, change topic.

title: Different peoples so you can know each other, not rank.
subtitle: One father, one mother, one measure of honor
then: Right after forbidding mockery and backbiting, Allah reminds all people they come from Adam and Hawwa. On the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet ﷺ said Allah had {trap}removed the pride of Jahiliyyah in forefathers.{/trap} Allah does not look at forms or wealth, but at {idea}hearts and deeds.{/idea}
now: A rishta conversation where the first question is which family, which tribe, which country. A workplace where some accents get promoted. A joke at a barbecue about another nationality. {idea}Names and flags are for recognizing each other.{/idea} {reward}Honor is measured somewhere else.{/reward}
old: Where I come from says something about how much I am worth.
new: My people and background help others know me, but my worth with Allah is only my taqwa.
try: Learn one real thing today about a colleague or neighbor from a different background. Ask them, and listen.

title: You submitted, but faith has not fully entered yet.
subtitle: Honest about where you are, with nothing lost
then: Some bedouins accepted Islam and at once claimed the rank of full believers. Ibn Kathir says {idea}they were not hypocrites,{/idea} only Muslims in whose hearts faith had not yet settled. They were told to claim what was true. {reward}Obey, and not one deed of yours will be cut short.{/reward}
now: You just started praying again, or you are new to Islam, and someone online asks if you are a strong believer. You feel you have to say yes. {idea}It is fine to say: I am trying, I am on the way.{/idea} {reward}Nothing you do is wasted while you grow.{/reward}
old: If my faith is not strong yet, my effort does not really count.
new: I can be honest about how far I have come, and every act of obedience is still fully counted.
try: Tell Allah honestly in your next prayer where your faith is right now, and ask Him to make it enter your heart.

title: The truthful believers: no doubt, and they give.
subtitle: What faith looks like when it is real
then: After the bedouins' claim, Allah describes who the real believers are. Ibn Kathir says {idea}their faith stayed firm, without doubt,{/idea} and they gladly gave their lives and their most precious wealth seeking His pleasure. {reward}They are truthful when they say they believe.{/reward}
now: Payday comes and you think about the charity you said you would give. Or a hard test comes, a diagnosis, a job loss, and your faith wobbles. {idea}The verse shows what steadies it: no going back on trust, and giving what you love.{/idea}
old: Believing is mostly something I feel and say.
new: Faith proves itself when I stay sure under pressure and give from what I value.
try: Give something today, money, time, or effort, that you would rather keep, quietly, for Allah.

title: Would you tell Allah about your own religion?
subtitle: He already knows what is in your heart
then: The bedouins kept insisting they had believed. {idea}Allah asks: will you inform Me of your religion?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says nothing in the heavens and earth escapes Him, not even a speck of dust. {trap}Announcing faith adds nothing to what He already sees.{/trap}
now: You post about your fast, your Quran streak, your umrah trip. Or you argue hard to prove you are a good Muslim to a relative. {idea}The One who matters already knows exactly where you stand.{/idea} Talk less about it, tend it more.
old: People need to know how religious I am.
new: Allah already knows my heart, so my energy goes into improving it, not announcing it.
try: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: Your Islam is not a favor you did anyone.
subtitle: Who owes whom for guidance
then: Ibn Abbas said Banu Asad came and told the Prophet ﷺ: we embraced Islam, and unlike other Arabs we never fought you. {trap}They counted their Islam as a favor to him.{/trap} The reply: {reward}Allah did you the favor by guiding you.{/reward} At Hunayn the Ansar answered the same way: Allah and His Messenger favored us.
now: You volunteer at the mosque every week and feel the committee should be more grateful. You pray, so you think Allah owes you an easy year. {idea}The ability to do any of it was given to you first.{/idea}
old: After all I do for the deen, I deserve some credit.
new: That I can serve at all is the favor, and it was done to me.
try: Before your next prayer, thank Allah for one specific moment He guided you back.

title: He knows the unseen and sees what you do.
subtitle: The last line of a surah about manners
then: The surah ends where it began: Allah hears, knows, and sees. It started with not rushing ahead of Him and {idea}ends reminding that He knows the unseen and sees all you do.{/idea} Every manner taught in between, voice, verifying, peace, no mockery, is done before His sight.
now: Alone in your car, alone with your phone, alone with a thought about someone. The manners of this surah are easy in a crowded room. {idea}They are real when no one but He is there.{/idea}
old: What I do privately is between me and no one.
new: Private is not unseen, so my manners do not switch off when the room empties.
try: Pick one manner from this surah and keep it tonight when you are alone, like no suspicious thoughts about anyone.
